This appeal coming on for orders this day, Justice Vi
 Rusia passed the following:
 Order

[1] The State of Madhya Pradesh and others have filed this appeal under Section 2(1) of M.P. Uchha Nyayalaya (Khand Nyaypeeth Ko Appeal Adhiniyam, 2005 against an interlocutory order dated 12.05.2023 passed by Writ Court in W.P. No.25932/2021.

sentences.text: The order is reproduced below:
Learned Senior counsel for the petitioners submits that petitioner No.2 has recently expired and prays for and is granted 3 weeks time to file appropriate application in that regard.
The parties are heard on I.A.No.2605/2023, which is an application for vacating the stay order dated 18.1.2023.

It is submitted by learned counsel for respondents No.1, 4 and 5 that respondent The State Of Madhya Pradesh vs Sureshchandra Yogi on 13 June, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/89523504/
3 No.4 after constructing the shops has issued NIT and thereafter the bidding process has been concluded and now only allotment of constructed shops to the bidders is left and due to the interim relief, further process is stopped.

sentences.text: Learned
Senior counsel for the petitioners submits that the interest of the petitioners shall be greatly and prejudicially affected in case the interim order is vacated.

It is further submitted that vacation of the interim order will result in multiplicity of proceedings as interests of third party shall also get involved which shall defeat the rights of the petitioners.
The contentions of the respondents are based entirely on merits which can be considered only at the time of adjudication of the petition on merits.
It is hence submitted that the application be rejected.

After having heard the learned counsel for the parties and having perused the record, in my opinion,
the interim order dated 18.1.2023 deserves to be suitably modified.
Respondents No.1, 4 and 5 are directed to earmark nine shops as against the interests of the petitioners in the present petition in the complex being constructed by them.
In respect of those shops the auction proceedings may continue but no allotment order be issued in respect of the successful bidder.
The allotment shall be subject to final decision of the petition.

It is further clarified that the auction proceedings may be finalized in respect of the other shops being constructed and the interim order dated 18.1.2023 shall not operate in respect of those shops.
If the petitioners or heirs of deceased petitioner No.2 are desirous of choosing any particular shop in the complex being constructed they may do so within a period of ten days from today.
With the aforesaid modification in the order dated 18.1.2023, the interim application bearing I.A.No.2605/2023, stands disposed off.
List for further consideration immediately after ensuing summer vacation.

[2] Shri Umesh Gajankush, learned Additional Advocate General for the appellants / State submits that the learned Writ Court has directed writ petitioners to choose particular 9 shops in the existing complex which could be allotted to them and because of which appellant No.2 is not in a position to finalize the auction of entire 49 shops.
The writ petitioners have no right to get particular shops by way of rehabilitation as they had already received the amount of compensation.
[3] It is further submitted that none of the writ petitioner participated in the auction proceedings and by submitting bid.

The respondent No.2 has received number of bids for all 49 shops, therefore, the direction given to the petitioners to select 9 shops would go against the interest of the bidders who had already quoted their bid money in the tender process.

[4] Shri Ashok Kumar Sethi, learned Senior Counsel for the respondent No.4 / writ petitioners submits that the present writ appeal is not maintainable as it is filed against the interlocutory order and even by way of interim order, no rights and liabilities of the parties have been decided.
The writ appeal may kindly be disposed off with the direction to the Writ Court to decide the writ petition on any date as early as possible.
Shri Sethi further submits that he will argue the writ petition finally as the pleadings are complete.

sentences.text: It is not the case that, the appellants are constructing the shops on a land where the writ petitioners were in possession.

Even,
if Writ Court comes to the conclusion that the writ petitioners are entitled for the allotment of shops under the rehabilitation policy although it has not been framed till date, the Writ Court shall pass suitable direction to the appellants for granting such rehabilitation compensation.
[6] Since the petitioners were tenants in the trust property, whether they are entitled to get the rehabilitation compensation is the issue which is to be decided by the Writ Court.

[7] The 49 shops had already been completed, the auction proceedings have been initiated in which none of the petitioner participated, therefore, the interim order dated 12.05.2023 is hereby set aside.
The Writ Appeal is hereby allowed.
No order as to cost.
